name: SWL Friday Night Raw

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("Friday Night Raw October 17,1997 Live From Oakland,California") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "{SWL} Friday Night Raw" (17 October 1997), Oakland, California.
evidence.note: The earliest surviving SWL card in this record: a three-way tag title match, two singles bouts and a title-creating main event.

eliminations.note: Pinned by Mex with a springboard sault, eliminating the Canadian Connection.
Pinned by the kick Ass order, who retained the SWL World Tag Team Titles.

matches.note: A three-way for the SWL World Tag Team Titles: Mex (billed the Tex Mex Connection) eliminated Shawn Masters (billed the Canadian Connection) before the champion kick Ass order (Mean Man and Basic Killer) eliminated Mex to retain.
Dave Dynamo pinned Carnage with a top-rope Shooting Star Press.
Night pinned the previously undefeated Manhunter with the Nightfall powerbomb to win the SWL United States Television Title.
American Heartthrob pinned Mr. Excellent with the Heartbreaker Heartpunch to become the first-recorded SWL World Brawler Champion.

notes: The promotion's earliest surviving card; a masked backstage figure (unidentified in this record) is referenced only as color, not minted.

name: In Your Face: Sharp Turn

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("In Your Face:Sharp-Turn February 28,1998 Live From San Francisco,California") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The fed's own Pay Per View broadcast script, subject "-=(SWL)=- In Your Face: Sharp Turn" (28 February 1998), San Francisco, California.
evidence.note: The promotion's first Pay Per View served in this record, with three title changes and the debut of its Sharp Turn gimmick match.

matches.note: Chaos Bill pinned the champion Night with the Hells Depth powerbomb to win the SWL World Brawler Title.
The Executioner beat Kevin Marcus with the Beheading, a DDT off the second rope.
Prodigy retained the SWL World Lightweight Title over Mr. Mainevent with a small package, after Mysterious's ringside tirade broke Mainevent's concentration.
Mr. Justice pinned the champion Insanity with a powerbomb to win the SWL World Heavyweight Title; a masked man attacked Justice moments later, laying him out with the title belt.

The first-ever "Sharp Turn" match: both men wrestled inside a moving trailer truck driven across the city to the arena. Basic Killer pinned Tony Arnold (billed as The Bat) with the Thrilla Killa spinning heel kick, after Basic Killer's tag partner Mean Man, driving the truck, powerbombed The Bat inside it.

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("**1st Anniversery Show** Friday Night Raw March 13,1998 Live From Miami,Florida") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.note: The promotion's own year-one retrospective, narrated on-air by its president, alongside a full card.

matches.note: Pain beat Black Hawk with a Tombstone piledriver to open the show.
The Ruiner beat The Executioner with a sunset flip in a number-one contender's match.

eliminations.note: Back body dropped over the top by Simon Prestwell.
Thrown over the top by The Ruiner and Simon Prestwell together.
Back body dropped over the top by The Ruiner.

Bone Harmen knocked Chaos Bill unconscious with a piledriver and the referee stopped the match; the promotion's president awarded Bone Harmen the win but ruled the SWL World Brawler Title did not change hands.
A non-title rematch of Sharp Turn's Sharp Turn match, cut short when Chaos Bill returned from injury to interfere on Tony Arnold's (billed The Bat) side; no decision was reached.

name: Warzone

date.source: The promotion's own Pay Per View broadcast carries this dateline (collected but not served); recapped in the fed's own newsletter, The Archive, issue 1 (27 June 1998).

evidence.source: The fed's own newsletter, subject "-=(SWL)=- The Archive" issue 1 (27 June 1998), recapping its Pay Per View, Warzone (21 June 1998, San Antonio, Texas -- date and venue per the promotion's own broadcast, collected but not served).
evidence.note: The fed's own second annual Pay Per View, recapped as a bare results digest in its own newsletter; only the bouts whose full rosters this record has independently structured are registered below.

matches.note: Billed in the fed's own newsletter results digest: "Prime Time defeated Harry Hender by pinfall."

notes: The fed's own newsletter results digest names four further bouts on this card (Hyper Man over Asics by DQ; Hardcore, billed as Insanity's later name, over Rob Bansin by DQ; Anthony Mislan over Kraze by DQ; Basic Killer and The Remedy over Gravedigger and Mass Destruction by pinfall) whose opponents (Asics, Rob Bansin, Kraze, The Remedy) are not independently structured in this record and so are not registered in matches -- the bouts live in the newsletter's own served text. Mass Destruction's own turn on Gravedigger to join the kick Ass order happened in the unregistered tag match.

name: SWL Monday Madness

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("Monday Madness December 1,1997 Live From Los Angeles,California") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "SWL Monday Madness" (2 December 1997), Los Angeles, California.
evidence.note: The earliest surviving Monday Madness card in this record, six weeks after the promotion's own debut card.

matches.note: Prodigy handed Viper his first loss with a top-rope Shooting Star Press.

Harley Robinson retained the SWL United States Television Title over Big Rob Styles; Demolisher tried to interfere for the kick Ass order but was ambushed and powerbombed on a chair by Tony Arnold before he could, while Raptor distracted the referee for Robinson's own corner.
Eric Scott upset The Violator, billed as wrestling his final match, with a surprise top-rope bulldog.

A non-title handicap match: Chaos Bill and Night, informally allied but not a stable, double-teamed the reigning SWL World Heavyweight Champion; Chaos Bill then double-crossed his own partner, shoving Night off the turnbuckles before pinning Mr. Excellent with the Hells Depth powerbomb. The title did not change hands.

The Reaper beat Kold Krush with the Reaper Stunner, in a match the broadcast's own commentary called sloppy.
Mysterious beat Simon Prestwell with the Top Rope Killer, noted on-air as coming off a 1-0 run in a rival league before quitting there.

Eliminated over the top rope by a drop kick from Biggy.

matches.note: The main event, billed by weight and height only (no title at stake); Biggy, managed by The Kid, won by eliminating both opponents.

notes: Biggy renames himself Kraze at the following Ring Masters broadcast; both his match participation here (order 5) and the appearances list above use the single record kraze-swl-1997b. A scheduled match between Gangsta and an opponent billed The Beast was awarded to Gangsta by forfeit when the broadcast reported The Beast had already left the promotion; this is recorded as a billed appearance rather than a match, and The Beast is not minted. Mr. Justice returns silently after an absence, declining an interview with Sunny; Basic Killer announces the kick Ass order's own return and his own spot in the promotion's upcoming pay-per-view main event; Mr. Justice, Basic Killer and Chaos Bill brawl at the close with no finish.

name: Ring Masters

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("Ring Masters March 22,1998 Live From Syracuse,New York") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "-=(SWL)=- Ring Masters" (22 March 1998), Syracuse, New York.
evidence.note: A signing swerve, a rival stable's debut, a title rename and a chaotic main event, nine days after the promotion's own 1st Anniversary show.

matches.note: Gravedigger beat Big Rob Styles with a reversed DDT. A follow-up loser-kisses-winner's-foot stipulation was aborted when Big Rob Styles's manager, Candy, hit Gravedigger with a chair.

Billed as Sniper's announced final match in the promotion. Officials broke up the match without a finish after a returning American Heartthrob climbed into the cage and brawled with Sniper; Cassaday escaped the cage during the confusion.

Tony Arnold (billed The Bat) substituted for an injured Chaos Bill. "Outlaw" Mark Slayer won a non-title match by reversing a powerbomb attempt into his own Outlaw Stunner, after his own second, John Merder, and JunkYard traded interference.

A SWL World Lightweight Title match; The Executioner entered as champion. A debuting authority figure, Biggy, stopped the match and ruled it a no-contest before a finish; the title did not change hands. Biggy then announced he wished to be called Kraze from that point forward.

Billed as a non-title brawl (Kraze carrying the SWL United States Television Title, Anthony Mislan managed by Luscious Lisa); the fight moved backstage via the Supremer-Tron, with the Rebels of Apocalypse and The Dog House both running in. No finish was shown.

Main event for the SWL World Heavyweight Title, Insanity entering champion with the Rebels of Apocalypse and Basic Killer with the entire kick Ass order. A mass brawl broke out at ringside; the referee called for the bell before a finish, and the title did not change hands. The Remedy appeared at the close wearing a kick Ass order t-shirt.

notes: Opens with a signing swerve: the promotion's president, Jerry Mack, brings out a debuting big man, The Remedy, sent by a rival federation to sabotage the deal; The Remedy powerbombs Jerry Mack before The Dog House (Chaos Bill, Tony Arnold and JunkYard) beat him down. This broadcast also confirms the Rebels of Apocalypse are Insanity's own stable, explicitly distinguished on-air from an unrelated, same-initialed group in a rival federation.

name: King of the Mats

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("King of the Mats May 24,1998 Live From San Francisco,California") and its Usenet posting date; billed on-air as a pay-per-view.

evidence.source: The fed's own pay-per-view broadcast script, subject "-=(SWL)=- King of the Mats" (25 May 1998), San Francisco, California.
evidence.note: A United States Television Title change, a World Heavyweight Title defense, a rival invader's promo, and a second Sharp Turn gimmick match.

matches.note: Gravedigger won the SWL United States Television Title from Mass Destruction with a low blow followed by a chokeslam, while his own manager, Miss Demeanor, distracted the referee on the apron.
Ecstasy was disqualified after retaliating on Prime Time's manager, Big D, who had clipped his leg from ringside; Prime Time hit Ecstasy with a chair after the bell.

Billed a rematch of a bout "a week" earlier, not otherwise surviving in this record. The referee stopped the match after Anthony Mislan's own leg broke against the ring stairs; Kraze was declared the winner, but the title did not change hands on a stoppage decision, leaving a thirty-day defense clause hanging over the champion.

A second Sharp Turn match, again fought inside a moving truck container driven to the arena. Tony Arnold (billed The Bat) helicoptered into the moving rig to aid a returning American Heartthrob, but Mean Man ran both Tony Arnold and Heartthrob down with a car outside the arena and abducted Tony Arnold, leaving Basic Killer to carry Heartthrob into the ring and pin him alone.

notes: A scheduled Andy Carter vs. The Ruiner match was scratched days before the show over The Ruiner's departure from the promotion; Andy Carter is recorded here as a billed appearance rather than a match, awarded the win by forfeit. A masked rival invader, Buff Dadio, interrupts the broadcast to threaten Kraze and "the Hardcore" (Insanity); he does not compete.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "-=(SWL)=- Friday Night Raw --Build up to Warzone--" (19 June 1998), Santa Fe, New Mexico.
evidence.note: The promotion's own build-up show for its second Pay Per View, two days out.

matches.note: Mental Case put Lake Walker away with the Mental Home Powerbomb after early domination from Walker.
Sheik Abdul hit the top-rope Arabian Splash for the win after both men were busted open, Membrane having gone through a ringside table.
Big Rob Styles ran in with a chair, knocking Mr. Mainevent out and controversially placing Gene Hoffman's hand over him for the pin after the referee was accidentally struck.

The whole kick Ass order jumped The Executioner before the bell meant anything; a mass brawl involving both locker rooms, a returning Remedy, a chair-shot ambush by Anthony Mislan, and a surprise return by American Heartthrob ran out the clock with no finish.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "-=(SWL)=- Monday Madness --Rodman Returns,The Bat Challenges,Kraze & Hardcore Vs. Mass Destruction and Mystery Opponent + More--" (29 June 1998), Raleigh, North Carolina.
evidence.note: The last surviving weekly broadcast in this record.

matches.note: J.V. and Hollywood interfered against Mr. Mainevent, crotching him on the ropes; The Executioner recovered to finish with the Be-Heading DDT from the second rope.
Non-title. Ryan Shaffer ran in with a chair and busted Mislan open, knocking out the referee in the process; once the referee revived, Gravedigger pinned the incapacitated Mislan.

Mass Destruction forfeited on The Remedy's behalf, citing a flight delay; immediately after, his own partner Hardcore chaired Kraze from behind, the Pain Killers ran in before further damage, and Hardcore announced over the arena speakers that he had joined the kick Ass order.

A cage match for a contract Tony Arnold himself put up. Elite X scaled the cage to back Rodman before the door was even locked; the masked man who ambushed Rodman alongside Arnold was unmasked as Basic Killer, and the show ran out of time with no finish shown.
